findings.screen: index.html and forms.ts — Title page details and missing-field feedback
findings.action: I would skip Title page details because it says Optional, then create my coursework document.

findings.screen: index.html — Model keys; job.html — completed document
findings.action: I would leave the optional model keys empty and download the resulting coursework PDF.
findings.observed: Implementation review only. The no-key explanation is inside collapsed Model keys and promises a source-linked draft. job.html shows Document ready and a Ready step for completed jobs; its explicit statement that Completed means only PDF compilation and that sections may be placeholders is inside collapsed Generation details. An outline warning and Outline PDF label do exist for the outline outcome.
findings.problem: I may interpret the ready messaging as a usable coursework document without opening technical details. Before starting without a key, I do not get a prominent explanation that I may need to write missing section content myself.

findings.action: I would edit two architecture sections and save the first, or follow a References link while still editing.
findings.observed: Implementation review only; no interactions performed. Each section has its own ordinary POST form, and References and Document status are normal links. Section forms lack data-busy; the supplied forms.ts adds no dirty-state tracking or navigation guard.
findings.problem: Only one section is submitted at a time, leaving my other unsaved correction vulnerable to being lost when the page navigates, with no visible indication of which edits remain unsaved.
findings.suggestion: Track dirty sections and offer Save all or a navigation warning that identifies the unsaved sections.
findings.reason: See triage.md for the invariant, mitigation and deferred scope.

findings.action: I would correct architecture prose while keeping the generated tables.

findings.problem: The only Save edit action destroys the tables I need to keep, so I cannot achieve my editing goal through the provided control even though the warning explains the loss.
findings.suggestion: Preserve generated tables when saving prose and provide a separate explicit action to remove them.
findings.reason: See triage.md for the invariant, mitigation and deferred scope.

findings.action: I would use Regenerate to try a better architecture section and compare it with my current draft.

findings.problem: A single click removes my saved draft before replacement text is available, with no visible way to recover it if regeneration is worse or fails.
findings.suggestion: Keep the current section as a recoverable version until I accept the regenerated replacement.
findings.reason: See triage.md for the invariant, mitigation and deferred scope.

findings.action: I would correct an architecture paragraph and click Save edit while keeping its generated tables.

findings.problem: I cannot accomplish the combined goal of correcting prose and keeping generated tables through this editor, even when my correction does not concern the tables.
findings.suggestion: Keep existing tables when saving prose and offer a separate explicit action to remove them.
findings.reason: See triage.md for the invariant, mitigation and deferred scope.

findings.action: I would edit two architecture sections, save the first, then follow a References link to check evidence.

findings.reason: See triage.md for the invariant, mitigation and deferred scope.

findings.action: I would check the completion indicator before deciding whether the PDF is ready for my review.

The download is labelled Draft PDF or Outline PDF.
findings.problem: The prominent readiness signals can lead me to interpret a full section count as verified content before I discover the qualification hidden below the downloads.
findings.suggestion: Show PDF compiled — content needs review beside the completion status and downloads, with the unresolved-gap count visible without expanding details.
findings.reason: See triage.md for the invariant, mitigation and deferred scope.

findings.action: I would read the privacy wording to decide whether submitting the project is acceptable.
findings.observed: Implementation review only. The landing page says Everything stays in this browser session, while its form posts uploaded files to /jobs and the collapsed Model keys section says Keys are encrypted on this server. The document page describes downloads as private to this browser.
findings.problem: I could mistake browser-bound access for local-only processing or storage, and submit source under an incorrect understanding of where it goes.
findings.heuristic: Match between system and the real world
findings.suggestion: Replace the session claim with a visible explanation that files are uploaded to the server and access is tied to this browser session, alongside the actual retention policy.
findings.reason: See triage.md for the invariant, mitigation and deferred scope.
